Badenoch replied: They can commission all the reports that they like, but it’s not going to change the situation, which is that Britain is out…

posts.title: Badenoch says Reform UK councillors not welcome back in Tory party, because she wants it to 'regenerate' with new people
posts.text: Q: [From Sophie Church from the Mail] Would you take back Reform UK MPs or councillors if they wanted to come back to the Conservative party? Badenoch said she wanted Reform UK voters to return to the Tories. She went on: Right now I am saying that we’re not taking back, certainly not the MPs who who left. I don’t…

posts.title: Badenoch claims she wants to prioritise tax cuts for businesses, not individuals, because those would boost growth
posts.text: Q: [From Ryan Sabey from the Sun] Would you prioritise unfreezing income tax thresholds? Badenoch replied: I do want taxpayers to get more of their money back, but we have to start off with those people paying the taxes that are actually halting economic growth. That’s why the tax cuts which we prioritise are for…

Q: [From Serena Barker-Singh from Sky News] Your party’s poll ratings are still lower than they were at the time of the last election. Your higher personal approval ratings have not helped the party. Are you worried the party is seen as toxic? Badenoch said that, when Barker-Singh started interviewing her, she was…

Q: [From Chris Mason from the BBC] How quickly could you implement the welfare cuts you propose? Within your first year in office? Badenoch replied: There will be many things that we can do on day one. We won’t be able to do everything on day one. Things like restoring the two child benefit cap, for instance – those…

Q: [From Christopher Hope from GB News] Why should people trust you when taxes went up under the last Conservative government? Badenoch said she did not approve of many of the tax rises implemented by the last government. She said Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, opposed those rises too; she said she recalled…

Badenoch is now taking questions. Q: [From ITV’s Carl Dinnen] You want to cut welfare spending, but you also want tax cuts for the rich. Do you think that is fair? Badenoch claimed her plans would help everyone. Young people would benefit from the cut in national insurance for young workers, she said.

posts.title: Badenoch tells Burnham getting people to stop playing loud music on trains 'job for ticket inspectors, not PM'
posts.text: Badenoch ended her speech with a jibe about Andy Burnham’s announcement yesterday about measures to stop people playing loud music on public transport. She said: It’s very easy to announce that you don’t like people making noise on trains. That is a job for ticket inspectors, not the prime minister. If Labour’s plan…

posts.title: Badenoch claims tax burden too high
posts.text: Badenoch says Britain needs tax cuts. We need to get out of the way of job creators who make our country richer. We need to encourage risk taking, wealth creation, enterprise. Britain’s tax burden has never been higher. You are taxed on the heating in your home. You’re taxed at the petrol pump filling up your car.…

Referring to Andy Burnham’s article published yesterday, Badenoch said: Andy Burnham wrote in The Times yesterday about the moral outrage of the current benefit system. But as far as I could work out, his answer is to spend even more on benefits.

posts.title: Badenoch says it would be 'unconscionable' to delay plan to raise defence spending to 3% of GDP until spending review next autumn
posts.text: Badenoch restates her call for benefit cuts to fund higher defence spending. I have said it before and I will say it again and again until I’m blue in the face: Britain’s national security is under threat. We need to cut welfare to fund defence. Cutting welfare to fund defence is our next challenge … John Healey…
Kemi Badenoch is giving her pre-budget speech now. So far, she has mostly stuck to the arguments briefed overnight. (See 8.47am and 9.29am.)

posts.title: Google suggests a workaround
posts.text: Google has updated its advice to those affected by its service disruption, with a possible workaround. It says: If feasible, the impacted customer may try to migrate their workload impacted to another available location (zone or region).
“A person familiar with the matter” has told Reuters that Revolut’s service outage was related to the Google Cloud service disruption (as we speculated a little while ago…)

There are also some reports of problems with other UK financial services firms today – perhaps a sign that the Google Cloud outage is causing wider problems. These chart from DownDetector show a rise in problems being reported by users of HSBC and Lloyds Banking Group this morning:

The service disruption at Google Cloud began just after 7am this morning UK time, or 23:08pm Pacific time last night. The disruption is focused at Google’s europe-west2 region, which is London. Other sites, such as Paris and Frankfurt, are not reporting problems.

Ticket sales are also being disrupted by the Google Cloud outage, according to Hertfordshire-based football club Hitchin Town. Hitchin Town (known as the Canaries) in soccer circles, say: There is currently a Europe wide issue with Google Cloud which hosts our ticketing site with @KaizenTicketing As a result our…
